scope: Final prose, reasoning, cross-references, highlights and rendered DOCX content/field completeness; numerical recomputation is covered by separate audits.
verdict: No critical contradiction or stale cross-reference; one targeted comparator clarification and two optional editorial cleanups.

primary_clarity_fix.issue: Unqualified local grain losses can be read as losses relative to conventional production. The new spatial statistics describe targeted-minus-uniform contrasts at the same reduction.

replacements.heading: Abstract
replacements.old_text: Mean grain losses nevertheless occurred on 37.60% of mapped rotation area.
replacements.replacement_text: Mean targeted-minus-uniform grain contrasts were negative on 37.60% of mapped rotation area.

replacements.heading: 5. Conclusions
replacements.old_text: Mean grain losses occurred on 37.60% of mapped rotation area and persisted in all twelve years on 21.34%.
replacements.replacement_text: Mean grain losses relative to uniform allocation occurred on 37.60% of mapped rotation area and persisted in all twelve years on 21.34%.
Targeting lowered grain on 37.60% of rotation area relative to uniform 50% cuts.

optional_editorial_cleanups.heading: 2.7.2. Annual quotas based on antecedent water availability
optional_editorial_cleanups.action: Delete the final paragraph; its continuous-state and GRACE-release statements are already established in preceding paragraphs.
optional_editorial_cleanups.exact_paragraph: The fixed-fraction histories select class-specific quotas, and the resulting annually switching strategies are simulated with their own continuous soil-water states. Availability of the corresponding GRACE release before sowing remains unverified; the comparisons use retrospective antecedent observations.

optional_editorial_cleanups.heading: 4.1. Marginal irrigation returns and spatial allocation
optional_editorial_cleanups.issue: The unqualified regional optimum label can imply optimality beyond the defined historical objective, and compensation mechanisms are asserted without evaluation. The next paragraph already supplies the local-safeguard implication.
optional_editorial_cleanups.action: Retain the distributional evidence, state the uniform comparator and omit the last two sentences.
optional_editorial_cleanups.replacement_paragraph: The spatial distribution sharpens this distinction between regional and local outcomes. Mean grain losses relative to uniform cuts occupy 37.60% of mapped rotation area, and losses persist in every comparison year on 21.34%. Gross gains of 10.568 Mt yr⁻¹ are partly offset by losses of 3.349 Mt yr⁻¹; the area-weighted median is zero despite a positive regional mean.

minor_typography.heading: 3.4. Spatial distribution and persistence of allocation effects
minor_typography.old_text: Local losses offset 31.69% of the gross positive contribution. (Figure 7d).
minor_typography.replacement_text: Local losses offset 31.69% of the gross positive contribution (Figure 7d).

passed_logic_checks: The six introduction paragraphs progress from production and water objectives through rotation dependence, spatial allocation, response evidence and information value to the management comparisons.
Methods place GRACE with environmental data, group the strategy definitions under 2.7 and retain metrics and spatial statistics last.
Figure 3 is located with estimation/evaluation definitions in Methods 2.5.
Results 3.3 introduces spatial heterogeneity and explicitly directs readers to new Section 3.4; annual quota selection follows in Section 3.5.
Discussion 4.1 incorporates the new loss-area and persistence results; Conclusions explicitly retain their regional/local implication.
The new spatial statistics are described as rotation-area-weighted model contrasts from 32 response units mapped to 3,641 cells; they are not treated as independent field observations.
The abstract, main production result and conclusion distinguish less loss relative to uniform cuts from higher production relative to conventional irrigation.
Discussion 4.5 retains retrospective testing limits, the 83.27% wheat grain error, the +3.108 t ha⁻¹ bias at 13% moisture and the unvalidated absolute regional dry-grain reference.
The storage-information result is bounded by the quota design and matched monitoring coverage, with no claim of general GRACE irrelevance or groundwater recovery.
